source.product: No real product. An invented warm-Japandi solid white-oak bedside nightstand with one drawer over an open niche, backing a synthetic stub listing.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround (codex-image), cropped at detected gutter boundaries, Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d (Meshy), should_texture+enable_pbr, target_polycount 24000
source.postProcessing: gltf-transform resize to 1024 px textures (resize only, no lossy re-encode, geometry untouched), then scripts/fit_glb.py 45 40 52
source.dimensionsVerifiedAt: Not a retail product; nothing external to verify against. Declared dimensions are what the mesh measures.
source.priceVerifiedAt: None. price_cents on the stub listing is invented demo data.

knownLimitations: Generic visual proxy, not a real SKU. It may only back a synthetic stub listing.

The target box was 45 x 40 x 52 cm. The generated mesh was too tall and too shallow for that, and the 10 percent anisotropy cap in fit_glb.py could not close the gap: fit_glb.py exited 1 with residuals of +1.25 cm width, +3.45 cm height, -3.45 cm depth. The declared dimensions above are what the file actually measures, not the original target, so the asset check passes only if the catalogue listing is written to these numbers.
fit_glb.py applied a per-axis scale at the full 10 percent anisotropy cap, so the mesh is stretched relative to what the generator produced.
The drawer front and its finger groove are texture and shallow relief only. Nothing opens.
The open shelf niche is reconstructed from a single front and three-quarter view; its interior depth and back face are inferred rather than observed.
The underside is generated, not observed. Expect approximate geometry there.
Visual quality has NOT been verified in a render. Only measurements, triangle count and byte size were checked against the file.
